To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have generated a model for ALS in Drosophilia that expresses human SOD1 in motor neurons and that this leads to progressive climbing deficits, defective neural circuit electophysiology, accumulation of SOD1 in neurons, a stress response in glia, and no neuronal loss.

transgenic expression of mutant human SOD1 in motor neurons of Drosophila leads to progressive motor deficits and electrophysiological abnormalities that are not accompanied by motor neuron loss, but do lead to glial stress.

we have developed a model of ALS in Drosophilia that expresses human SOD1 in motor neurons, that this model recapitulates the motor neuron injury and glial stress response seen in ALS, and that this injury is not associated with neuronal loss or oligomerization of mutant SOD1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new animal model of familial ALS, which will allow us to investigate molecular mechanisms of disease and to develop new treatments.
understanding the mechanisms that cause motor neuron degeneration in ALS.
the development of a model for amyotrophy lateral sclerosis (ALS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SOD1 is toxic to motor neurons, but not to all cells.
the SOD mutation causes motor neuron damage by a mechanism that is not understood.
the Drosophila model recapitulates some features of human ALS, but not all.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an in vivo model for motor neuron injury by SOD in ALS.
we have generated a new model of ALS that allows us to dissect the cellular mechanisms of disease.
we have generated and analyzed the first Drosophila model of ALS, which recapitulates many features of the human disease, and which will be a valuable tool for future studies of ALS pathogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SOD1 toxicity in motor neurons is not due to loss of function but rather is due to a dominant toxic gain of function
the SOD-1 mutation is toxic to motor neurons and that it is not necessary to have motor neuron loss to see the effects of the mutation.
we have shown that human SOD1 can cause motor dysfunction in a model organism, Drosophila, that recapitulates many of the features of ALS in humans.
